opp_tight_l5.label: opponent last-5 DRtg 3+ better than its season (vs neutral band)

opp_leaky_l1.label: opponent last-game DRtg 10+ worse (vs neutral band)

opp_tight_l1.label: opponent last-game DRtg 10+ better (vs neutral band)

vac_large.label: regulars out total 20+ prior PPG (vs none)

hot_last1.label: after a hot last game (>=1.25x avg)

min_dn3.label: recent minutes trend down (last-5 3+ below season)

role_demoted.label: recently demoted from the starting five

caveats: Associational, not causal. A player's response to 'top scorer out' mixes role (second option vs role player), minutes, lineups and opponent adjustments; it is a pattern in his games, not a trait he carries to another team.

Teammates out is observed from the box score of the game itself (inactive or non-coach DNP); it is knowable at about tip-off, not days ahead. Team changes between periods are not modelled: a player who moved teams has a different set of teammates in the two periods.

One held-out season is short. Persistence of per-player significance is low-powered; the correlation, calibration slope and sign repeat are the fairer reads. Cross-season correlations use players with 10+ games on both sides in both periods, so rare conditions (3+ rest days, role changes, best/worst-5 defence) can be tested for few players only.
Odd-even and random halves share the same seasons: they overstate persistence (team-specific and spell-specific effects). We only call something 'persistent' if it also shows across seasons.

The conditions overlap (rest 0 = second night of a back-to-back; best-5 within best-10; vacuum measures): 28 conditions x 5 outcomes = 140 cells per segment are tested. Persistence uses BH q < 0.10 over those cells; flags use a permutation expectation per cell, not a multiplicity correction across cells.

Event outcomes (1.25x, 1.5x, 2.0x, +10) are sparse per player (a 1.5x night is about 16% of games, 2.0x about 4%): their per-player intervals are wide and most shrink to the league mean. Pp effects scale with a player's base rate, so we report a partial correlation controlling for it.

The effect against the prior season-to-date average inherits the baseline lag found in BIG_NIGHTS.md (after a hot game or a minutes increase the season average is stale). Those two conditions are at least partly 'average is out of date', not response.

The persistent responders are largely the same names under 'top scorer out' and '20+ PPG teammate out' (role players who become primary options when a team's leading scorer sits); their effect is a role effect on their team, not a portable trait, and players who changed teams between periods are compared across different casts.
Stars: top 25 and top 10 are always thin (25 and 10 players) and reuse the top 50 EB parameters; only top 100 and top 50 can be ranked.
2026-27 and the pooled spans that include it are provisional. The 2023-24 + 2024-25 span is an internal training span, not an app timespan (rows carry `aux_training_span`).
Not available: sportsbook lines (so no edge calculation), defender matchups, referee crews, pregame injury report beyond the inactive list, play-by-play.

flag_rules.strong: shrunk 95% interval excludes 0 (flag) or excludes the league mean (flag_vs_league), n >= 15 on both sides
flag_rules.watch: shrunk 90% interval excludes the target, not strong
flag_rules.note: use flag_vs_league for who responds differently; flag (!= 0) restates the league mean when tau is about 0

insights.title: Show 'responds to the top scorer being out' for players who clear the bar
insights.text: The one player-specific pattern that persists across seasons: players differ in how much they gain when their team's top scorer is out (dev: temporal r +0.39 [+0.17, +0.57], tau 1.4 pts around a league mean of +2.0). Show the shrunk effect with its interval and n for players flagged vs league (strong or watch), never the raw difference; wording 'associated with'; trigger from the inactive list.

insights.title: Do not ship player-specific cards for the noise conditions
insights.text: Back-to-back and rest days, defence tier, pace, opponent recent form, minutes down, 3+ rest and role change have no player-specific effect that survives out of sample (and nothing measurable at all for most of them). Show the league-level effect and a 'tested, no player pattern persists' note instead of a player ranking.

insights.title: Label within-season-only patterns as 'this season only' or hide them
insights.text: Home/away, hot game, bounce-back (dev), minutes up, early vs late, worst-5 defence and the any-teammate-out measures are consistent within a season but do not predict the next season. If shown at all, mark 'this season, may reflect the current team situation', and never as a trait.

insights.title: Stars: league-level effects only
insights.text: No condition has a persistent player-specific effect among the top 100 / 50, and the cross-season test is mostly under-powered for them. For stars show the pooled league effects from BIG_NIGHTS, not individual responder lists.

insights.title: Use shrunk estimates and the vs-league flag
insights.text: `flag` (differs from zero) is a statement about the league mean whenever tau is about 0. Use `flag_vs_league` (+ shrunk interval + n both sides) for who responds differently, and show the reliability (EB reliability about 0.3 to 0.45 for the persistent cells: a player's raw estimate is mostly noise).

insights.title: Show flagged-vs-chance beside any list
insights.text: Print the expected-by-chance count beside the flagged count (about 0 for vs-league flags under the permutation null) and the persistence verdict of the condition; do not rank a condition whose verdict is noise.

insights.title: Hide 2026-27 per-player condition rows
insights.text: 2026-27 has at most a few players with 3+ games on both sides of a condition; the held-out check is empty. Mark provisional or hide.

insights.title: Do not present these as betting edges
insights.text: The effects are in points against the player's own prior average, not against a line; league-wide parts are already visible to the market. Use as context ('responds more than most when X'), not as a bet.
